tasks.title: Create src/lib/eligibility.ts (taxonomy + classify + matches)
tasks.description:
Create a new module at src/lib/eligibility.ts that owns the entire eligibility tag system. Export all of the following:

TYPES:
- `type Tag` — string-literal union of all 26 valid tag values: 6 flat tags ("Need-Based", "Merit-Based", "First-Generation", "State-Specific", "Athletic", "Creative/Arts") plus 20 category tags using the "Category:Value" shape (port the exact strings from `scripts/tag-eligibilities.ts` lines 23–61 — these are the source of truth for current tag names: Gender-Specific:Women, Gender-Specific:Men, Race/Ethnicity:African American/Black, Race/Ethnicity:Hispanic/Latino, Race/Ethnicity:Jewish, Disability/Health:Vision, Disability/Health:Hearing, Disability/Health:Learning Disability, Disability/Health:Cancer/Chronic Illness, Disability/Health:Mental Health, Major-Specific:STEM/Engineering, Major-Specific:Business/Accounting, Major-Specific:Healthcare/Nursing, Major-Specific:Arts/Theater, Major-Specific:Agriculture, Major-Specific:Law, Major-Specific:Architecture, Military/Veterans:Active Duty, Military/Veterans:Veteran, Military/Veterans:Military Dependent).
- `type EligibilityFlatTag` — the 6 flat tags only (subset of Tag).
- `type EligibilityCategory` — string-literal union of category names: "Gender-Specific" | "Race/Ethnicity" | "Disability/Health" | "Major-Specific" | "Military/Veterans".
- `type TagGroup` — `{ category: string; tags: readonly Tag[] }`.

VALUE EXPORTS:
- `const ELIGIBILITY_FLAT_TAGS: readonly EligibilityFlatTag[]` — the 6 flat tags as a readonly tuple (port from src/data/scholarships.ts lines 57–60).
- `const ELIGIBILITY_CATEGORIES` — record/object mapping each EligibilityCategory to its readonly array of sub-option strings (port from src/data/scholarships.ts lines 64–70).
- `const ALL_TAGS: readonly Tag[]` — full taxonomy as a flat array (flat tags + every "Category:SubOption" pairing). Derived from ELIGIBILITY_FLAT_TAGS + ELIGIBILITY_CATEGORIES so adding a category sub-option flows through automatically.
- `const TAG_GROUPS: readonly TagGroup[]` — UI-renderable groupings: one group with `{ category: "flat", tags: ELIGIBILITY_FLAT_TAGS }` first (or whatever convention matches existing UI consumers — check filter-sheet.tsx for the rendering shape before deciding), then one group per EligibilityCategory.

FUNCTION EXPORTS:
- `function isEligibilityFlatTag(tag: string): tag is EligibilityFlatTag` — type predicate. Port behaviour from src/data/scholarships.ts lines 75–77.
- `function getEligibilityCategory(tag: string): EligibilityCategory | null` — port from scholarships.ts lines 80–83. Returns the substring before ":" if present, else null.
- `function getEligibilitySubOption(tag: string): string | null` — port from scholarships.ts lines 86–89.
- `function getEligibilityTagLabel(tag: string): string` — port from scholarships.ts lines 92–94.
- `function classify(eligibilityText: string): Tag[]` — runs a private TAG_RULES table (port verbatim the 32 regex entries from scripts/tag-eligibilities.ts lines 23–61, but with the tag literal typed as Tag). Returns deduplicated tags in declaration order. Returns [] for empty/no-match input.
- `function matches(scholarship: { eligibilityTags: readonly Tag[] }, selected: readonly Tag[]): boolean` — empty selection returns true; otherwise group selected tags by category (using `getEligibilityCategory(tag) ?? tag` as group key — flat tags become their own group); a scholarship matches if every group has at least one member present in scholarship.eligibilityTags. Port semantics from src/lib/scholarship-utils.ts lines 14–38 (matchesEligibilityTags), tightening the selectedTags type from string[] to readonly Tag[].

IMPLEMENTATION RULES:
- Single source of truth: ALL_TAGS and TAG_GROUPS derive from ELIGIBILITY_FLAT_TAGS + ELIGIBILITY_CATEGORIES, not separately listed. Tag literal union is the only place where the full enumeration appears.
- The 32 regex rules in TAG_RULES are private to the module (not exported).
- No external dependencies beyond TypeScript/React types — pure logic.
- Default to no comments unless WHY is non-obvious.

See PRD §Implementation Decisions / New module.
acceptance: type Tag — string-literal union of all 26 valid tag values.
type TagGroup — { category: string; tags: readonly Tag[] } describing UI-renderable groupings.
const ALL_TAGS: readonly Tag[] — the full taxonomy as a flat array.
const TAG_GROUPS: readonly TagGroup[] — the taxonomy organized for UI rendering with category headers plus their child tags. Flat tags sit in their own group at the top.
function classify(eligibilityText: string): Tag[] — runs the rule set against free-text eligibility prose and returns deduplicated tags. Pure; returns [] for empty or unmatched input.

function matches(scholarship: { eligibilityTags: Tag[] }, selected: readonly Tag[]): boolean — implements the prior PRD's composition rules: empty selection passes everything through; non-empty selection requires AND across categories and OR within a category.
The 32 regex rules previously inlined in the script move into the module's private rule table.
tasks.notes: getEligibilityCategory tightened to return EligibilityCategory | null (also guards prefix is real category — stray 'Foo:Bar' → null). TAG_GROUPS uses { category: 'flat', tags: ELIGIBILITY_FLAT_TAGS } as first group; current filter-sheet.tsx iterates ELIGIBILITY_FLAT_TAGS + ELIGIBILITY_CATEGORIES directly so TAG_GROUPS is awaiting a UI consumer. matches accepts readonly Tag[]. classify('') → []; deduplication preserves first-seen declaration order.

tasks.title: Add src/lib/__tests__/eligibility.test.ts (classify, matches, round-trip)
tasks.description:
Create the test file at src/lib/__tests__/eligibility.test.ts with full PRD coverage of the eligibility module.

IMPORTS:
```
import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"
import { classify, matches, ALL_TAGS, type Tag } from "../eligibility"
```

CASES (per PRD §Testing Decisions):

1. classify text-based cases:
   - `classify("Be a graduating senior… 3.75 GPA… financial need")` returns a list including "Need-Based" AND "Merit-Based". Use `expect(result).toContain("Need-Based")` and `expect(result).toContain("Merit-Based")`.
   - `classify("")` returns [] (empty array).
   - `classify("Open to all students")` returns [] (no rule matches).

2. matches semantics:
   - `matches({ eligibilityTags: [] }, [])` returns true (empty selection passthrough).
   - `matches({ eligibilityTags: ["Need-Based"] }, ["Merit-Based"])` returns false (tag not present).
   - `matches({ eligibilityTags: ["Need-Based", "Merit-Based"] }, ["Need-Based"])` returns true.
   - `matches({ eligibilityTags: ["Race/Ethnicity:Hispanic/Latino", "Need-Based"] }, ["Race/Ethnicity:African American/Black", "Race/Ethnicity:Hispanic/Latino", "Need-Based"])` returns true (OR within Race/Ethnicity category, AND with flat Need-Based group).

3. Round-trip integrity:
   - For a corpus of plausible eligibility prose that exercises multiple rules, every tag returned by classify is included in ALL_TAGS. At minimum: take the union of `classify(text)` over a fixture array of 5–10 representative eligibility strings (mix of flat-only, category-only, and mixed) and assert every output tag is in ALL_TAGS via `expect(ALL_TAGS).toContain(tag)`.

Use describe blocks per group. Aim for >=10 individual test assertions total.

DO NOT modify the eligibility module itself or any other files. Tests only.
acceptance: classify("Be a graduating senior… 3.75 GPA… financial need") returns a list including "Need-Based" and "Merit-Based".
classify("") and classify("Open to all students") return [].
matches({ eligibilityTags: [] }, []) returns true.
matches({ eligibilityTags: ["Need-Based"] }, ["Merit-Based"]) returns false.
matches({ eligibilityTags: ["Need-Based", "Merit-Based"] }, ["Need-Based"]) returns true.

matches({ eligibilityTags: ["Race/Ethnicity:Hispanic/Latino", "Need-Based"] }, ["Race/Ethnicity:African American/Black", "Race/Ethnicity:Hispanic/Latino", "Need-Based"]) returns true (OR within category, AND across).
Round-trip integrity: every tag returned by classify is included in ALL_TAGS.
tasks.notes: 8 vitest cases (3 classify, 4 matches, 1 round-trip), 8/8 pass. Round-trip fixture exercises flat-only, single-category, multi-category, mixed prose; `all.size > 0` guard against silent-empty regression. Used `as const` literals on inline matches calls; Tag[] annotation only where TS won't narrow.
